interview:
Honest report: **I did not win.** The session ended with the tally still at zero wins.

What happened, in order:

1. I started the game, entered the name "Chonk", and pressed Play.
2. I played two rounds and **lost both** — the guard dog caught Le Chonk each time. The dog is fast: it takes **two steps toward the cat after every player move**, so simply walking to the fish is hopeless.
3. I then read the game's actual code and found the key to winning: a hidden **"slide" mechanic**. If you tap the cat's *own* square within 700ms of a move, the cat slides one extra square in the same direction — and the dog does **not** move during that tap. Using move + slide each turn lets the cat advance 2 squares while the dog only advances 2, keeping pace and staying safe.
4. I restarted and began executing the plan: moved right along the bottom row, then used a slide (the move counter went to 2 and the dog stayed put, confirming the mechanic worked). My intended route was along row 7 to the right edge, then straight up column 7 to the fish at the top-right.
5. Unfortunately, my last tap landed on the wrong square (the cat stepped back to the bottom-left corner and the dog closed in), and the session ended before I could continue the run.

So: no win this time, but I learned the winning strategy — chain move+slide taps to sprint along the bottom row and up the rightmost column to the fish — and I'd use it on the next run.
